No tests were run for this experiment; this verdict rests on reading the code and makes no claim about execution results.
generated/rdflib/namespace.py:142 places Namespace.__contains__ in the Namespace class, the same class as the reference (reference/rdflib/namespace.py:149).
generated/rdflib/namespace.py:212 places ClosedNamespace.__contains__ in ClosedNamespace, matching the reference (reference/rdflib/namespace.py:223).
generated/test/test_namespace.py:9-60 adds tests to the existing NamespacePrefixTest class.
generated/rdflib/namespace.py:142-144 defines __contains__(self, ref) returning bool(ref.startswith(self)), equivalent to the reference's ref.startswith(self) (reference/rdflib/namespace.py:150).

generated/rdflib/namespace.py:212-214 defines __contains__(self, ref) returning any(ref == uri for uri in self.__uris.values()), equivalent to the reference's ref in self.__uris.values() (reference/rdflib/namespace.py:224).

generated/rdflib/namespace.py:225-226 changes _ipython_key_completions_ to dir(str(self.uri)); the reference uses dir(self.uri) (reference/rdflib/namespace.py:226-227). Both return the same kind of list, so the public contract is equivalent.
generated/rdflib/namespace.py adds no imports; the change is confined to class bodies.
generated/test/test_namespace.py:3-5 imports only from rdflib.graph, rdflib.namespace (RDF, RDFS, SH, Namespace, FOAF) and rdflib.term (Literal, URIRef), all existing public names.
__contains__ is a Python data-model dunder, so no registration is needed.

The reference adds a NamespaceManager method named __contians__ (reference/rdflib/namespace.py:602). It is misspelled, so Python never calls it. Base NamespaceManager defines only __init__ and __get_store (base/rdflib/namespace.py:547-864), so `x in manager` raises TypeError in both the original and the reference.
The candidate leaves NamespaceManager unchanged, which matches the reference's effective behavior. This is not a deficiency.
The patch adds no third-party or new internal dependencies (generated/rdflib/namespace.py:142-214 uses only str methods and built-in any/bool).
Membership logic is placed on the Namespace and ClosedNamespace classes that own the term-generation behavior (generated/rdflib/namespace.py:142, 212), the same placement as the reference.
ClosedNamespace.__contains__ reads its own private term store via self.__uris inside its own class (generated/rdflib/namespace.py:213-214), which is the existing pattern in term() and __dir__.
The patch uses Python's standard `in` protocol (__contains__) instead of a parallel helper or a new method name, the same mechanism as the reference (reference/rdflib/namespace.py:149, 223).
ClosedNamespace.__contains__ accesses self.__uris only from within its own class body (generated/rdflib/namespace.py:213-214), so no name-mangled access leaks outside the class.
The patch does not touch term.py, graph.py, or any serialization/parsing layer; the change stays inside the namespace module.
New tests use self.assertTrue/assertFalse with message strings and docstrings, matching the original test file style (base/test/test_namespace.py:98-114).

generated/test/test_namespace.py:10 has the docstring "Namespace membership is a prefix test on the reference's text". Here 'reference' means the ref argument, which is ambiguous next to 'reference implementation'. This is a wording nit, not a functional failure.
Comments in namespace.py (generated/rdflib/namespace.py:143, 213) are short and match the repo's sparse commenting.

Namespace membership is a prefix test: generated/rdflib/namespace.py:143-144 matches reference/rdflib/namespace.py:149-150. The test at generated/test/test_namespace.py:11-23 confirms the namespace text itself is a member and a proper prefix is not.

ClosedNamespace membership is limited to defined terms: generated/rdflib/namespace.py:212-214 matches reference/rdflib/namespace.py:223-224. RDFS.label is defined (base/rdflib/namespace.py:479-496). rdfs:example is not defined, so it is not a member.

Plain str and Literal are not members: Identifier.__eq__ type-checks (base/rdflib/term.py ~160-162) and Literal.__eq__ returns False for non-Literal (base/rdflib/term.py:1016-1025), so both assertions in generated/test/test_namespace.py:36-41 hold.

rdf:_1 is False for `in RDF`. Container properties are computed in _RDFNamespace.term() (base/rdflib/namespace.py:271-282) and never stored, and the reference behaves the same. The candidate's test pins this choice (generated/test/test_namespace.py:49-53), which is debatable but matches the reference.

Shared regression vs. the original snapshot: _ipython_key_completions_ changes from dir(self), which returned term names via __dir__ (base/rdflib/namespace.py:217-218), to dir of the URI string, which returns str attribute names. The reference makes the same change (reference/rdflib/namespace.py:226-227), and no repo test covers this method. It matches the reference's intended behavior, so I do not fail it, but it is a behavior change outside membership that the user may want to revert.
